Q: What does ARIMA stand for in time series analysis?
What are the three components of an ARIMA model and what do they represent?

O.a: AR (autoregressive), I (integrated), MA (moving average); they represent the model's dependence on past values, differencing to achieve stationarity, and dependence on past forecast errors, respectively
O.b: AR (autoregressive), IR (integrated regression), MA (moving average); they represent the model's dependence on past values, regression on exogenous variables, and dependence on past forecast errors, respectively
O.c: AR (adaptive regression), I (independent), MA (moving average); they represent the model's adaptability to changing patterns, the independence of observations, and smoothing of past errors, respectively
O.d: AR (autoregressive), I (interpolation), MA (mean average); they represent the model's dependence on past values, the use of interpolation to fill gaps, and averaging of past values, respectively

Q: What is the role of differencing (the 'I' component) in an ARIMA model?

O.a: To make the time series stationary by removing trends and seasonality
O.b: To improve the accuracy of the model by reducing noise
O.c: To forecast future values based on past trends
O.d: To introduce exogenous variables into the model

Q: How are the parameters (p, d, q) of an ARIMA(p,d,q) model determined?

O.a: Through statistical methods like ACF and PACF analysis, along with model selection criteria like AIC or BIC
O.b: By arbitrarily selecting values that seem reasonable
O.c: By using a fixed set of predetermined values
O.d: By minimizing the sum of squared errors

Q: What do the parameters p, d, and q represent in an ARIMA(p, d, q) model?

O.a: p: order of the autoregressive (AR) model, d: degree of differencing, q: order of the moving average (MA) model
O.b: p: period of seasonality, d: degree of differencing, q: number of lags
O.c: p: number of parameters in the AR model, d: data size, q: number of errors
O.d: p: number of past observations to consider, d: data delay, q: quantity of future observations to predict

Q: What is the purpose of using ACF (Autocorrelation Function) and PACF (Partial Autocorrelation Function) plots in ARIMA modeling?

O.a: To identify the orders (p, q) of the AR and MA components of the model
O.b: To determine the degree of differencing (d)

Q: What are some common model selection criteria used to evaluate ARIMA models?

O.a: AIC (Akaike Information Criterion) and BIC (Bayesian Information Criterion)
O.b: RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) and MAE (Mean Absolute Error)

Q: What is a key assumption of ARIMA models?

O.a: The time series data is stationary or can be made stationary through differencing
Seasonal ARIMA model which considers seasonal patterns in data
O.b: Simple ARIMA model which ignores seasonal patterns
O.c: An ARIMA model with only autoregressive components
O.d: An ARIMA model that uses machine learning

Q: What are some limitations of ARIMA models?

O.a: They may not accurately capture non-linear relationships in data
O.b: They assume the data is stationary or can be transformed into stationarity
O.c: They can be computationally intensive, particularly with long time series or complex models
